content.value_statement: Animation regressions can make interfaces feel slow, distracting, or inaccessible. This skill reviews motion changes against strict duration, easing, performance, and accessibility standards.
actual_capabilities: Reviews UI motion changes for purpose, frequency, and interaction feel.
Flags slow timing, weak easing, wrong transform origins, and unnecessary motion.
Checks animation performance risks, including layout properties and main-thread motion.
Evaluates reduced-motion handling and hover motion gating.
Produces a findings table and an explicit Approve or Block verdict.
limitations: It reviews motion quality and does not implement fixes by itself.
It depends on provided diffs or code context and may miss issues outside shared files.
It cannot measure actual frame rates without runtime profiling or device testing.
It uses opinionated standards, so brand-specific motion may need human judgment.

use_cases.title: Pull Request Motion Review
use_cases.description: Catch slow, inaccessible, or expensive motion before a frontend pull request merges.

use_cases.title: Design System Quality Gate
use_cases.description: Keep timing, easing, transform origins, and accessibility rules consistent across shared components.

use_cases.title: Interaction Design Validation
use_cases.description: Validate that proposed motion supports state, feedback, and spatial understanding without distracting frequent users.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Animation Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when reviewing one component or a small motion change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this UI animation change for motion quality. Focus on purpose, duration, easing, accessibility, and whether it should ship.

prompt_templates.title: Pull Request Motion Gate
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before merging a pull request with animation changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the motion changes in this pull request. Cite file and line references, list concrete fixes, and end with Approve or Block.

prompt_templates.title: Design System Motion Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when several components share timing, easing, or interaction patterns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this component library update against the animation standards. Compare repeated patterns, flag inconsistent motion, and suggest reusable timing and easing rules.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Gesture Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for gesture-driven interfaces or performance-sensitive motion.
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a strict review of these gesture and animation changes. Evaluate interruptibility, GPU-only properties, reduced motion, hover gating, and high-frequency interaction risk.

output_examples.input: A pull request adds a dropdown animation that feels slow and ignores reduced-motion settings.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a findings table with slow timing, missing reduced-motion handling, and a Block verdict until both are fixed.

output_examples.input: A design systems team wants a motion quality pass before merging a toast update.
output_examples.output: The skill checks purpose, interruptibility, timing, and performance risks, then lists approval criteria for the merge.

output_examples.input: A gesture-driven drawer change needs review for polish and responsiveness.
output_examples.output: The skill reviews whether the motion remains interruptible, avoids main-thread performance issues, and matches gesture expectations.

best_practices: Provide the diff, affected components, and expected interaction frequency.
Include screenshots or recordings when motion feel is central to the review.
Ask for a final Approve or Block decision with file and line citations.
anti_patterns: Using the skill for general code review unrelated to animation.
Requesting approval without sharing the motion code or user interaction context.
Treating every decorative animation as acceptable because it is visually pleasing.

faq.question: Does this skill write animation code?
faq.answer: It is mainly a review skill. It can suggest concrete fixes, but its purpose is to judge motion quality.

faq.question: What kinds of animation does it review?
faq.answer: It reviews UI transitions, gestures, hover motion, popovers, modals, toasts, drawers, and related accessibility behavior.

faq.question: Can it review Framer Motion changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can flag high-risk shorthand properties, interruptibility problems, and motion that may drop frames under load.

faq.question: Does it require runtime profiling?
faq.answer: No. It can review code statically, but runtime profiling is still useful for frame-rate and device-specific issues.

faq.question: How strict is the verdict?
faq.answer: The skill defaults to blocking motion that feels slow, lacks purpose, harms performance, or ignores reduced-motion needs.

faq.question: Is it useful for design systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps teams keep timing, easing, origins, and accessibility rules consistent across shared components.
